title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Priya Desai
description: Motivation: observed periodic tail latency spikes in the continuous batcher under mixed-tenancy workloads due to unbounded queueing and head-of-line starvation from large long-running requests. This PR tunes the scheduler to improve queueing behavior and fairness, adds starvation prevention, enforces per-request queue timeouts, and exposes new telemetry for monitoring. Changes include: 1) switch scheduler core policy to a weighted deficit-round-robin (WFQ-like) variant to respect tenant weights while keeping high throughput; 2) introduce age-based priority boost to prevent starvation of low-weight or long-waiting requests; 3) add per-request queue_timeout_ms and global queue_length_high/low watermarks with backpressure signals to upstream routers; 4) introduce a soft preemption hook that allows small requests to bypass a draining large batch when age threshold crossed; 5) expose metrics: continuous_batcher.queue_wait_ms (histogram), continuous_batcher.starvation_count, continuous_batcher.backpressure_events, and config knobs via runtime flags and console; 6) add unit and integration tests and perf-canary config to validate no-regressions in throughput and improvements in P95/P99 under mixed workloads; 7) docs and release notes for operators including recommended knob defaults. Testing: local unit tests cover scheduler invariants and timeout paths; integration tests run in perf-canary showing median latency +1% but P99 reduced by ~18% and starvation_count dropped to near-zero for tested mixes; CI full suite green. Rollout plan: feature-flagged, staged rollout to Dedicated pools with canary enabled and dashboard alerts. Linear: ENG-5123 (scheduler fairness tuning), ENG-4987 (continuous-batcher starvation incidents). Checklist: - [x] Design and perf analysis - [x] Implementation - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration/perf runs - [x] Docs and config defaults - [x] Reviewer feedback addressed
